plain_summary: Niacin (nicotinic acid) has a moderate risk of side effects in older people and does not work for dementia.

medicine_groups.name: Niacin (nicotinic acid)
medicine_groups.note: Niacin is also called nicotinic acid. Nicotinamide (also called niacinamide) is a different compound and does not count. Low-dose vitamin B3 inside a multivitamin does not count. No Australian brand is listed, so a history shows the ingredient name.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when the person is aged 65 or older and niacin (nicotinic acid) is supplied as a single medicine. If age is missing and the supply otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is 65 or older. A recorded age below 65 gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why niacin was taken (for example a cholesterol problem or a vitamin deficiency), the dose actually taken, and niacin bought over the counter as a supplement.
ask_the_gp: Whether niacin is still needed and whether a different treatment could be used, taking into account the reason it was started.
